title: Charissa Thompson's Ex-Husband Joke Steals TNF Postgame
htmlContent:
The Chicago Bears gave Soldier Field plenty to cheer about on Thursday night with a hard-fought 30-24 win over the New England Patriots. But by the time the postgame show wrapped, the most talked-about moment of the evening may not have come from the field at all. It came from the studio desk, courtesy of Amazon Prime Video host Charissa Thompson.

A Postgame Show With a Twist

Thompson steered the Thursday Night Football postgame coverage the way she does every week, guiding her fellow analysts through the key plays, turning points and takeaways from the matchup. Breakdowns like these usually follow a familiar rhythm. This one took a detour.

In the middle of the discussion, Thompson turned to her co-hosts with a line nobody saw coming:

"I thought you were going to make me rank my good, better, best ex-husbands, and they're all bad."

CHARISSA THOMPSON WITH AN ALL-TIMER ON THE POSTGAME SHOW: “I THOUGHT YOU WERE GONNA MAKE ME RANK MY GOOD, BETTER, BEST EX-HUSBANDS, AND THEY’RE ALL BAD.” 💀💀💀 https://t.co/zAvC5rpRnH

— MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 23, 2026

It was a quick aside, delivered with a straight face, and it landed perfectly. In a single sentence, Thompson managed to make a routine football recap feel like a conversation among friends.

Why the Moment Worked

Was a postgame football show the most obvious place for a crack about failed marriages? Probably not. But that is exactly why it resonated. Sports broadcasts are often polished to the point of feeling rehearsed, and viewers rarely see hosts let their guard down on air.

Thompson's joke was a reminder that the people on the other side of the screen have lives, histories and a sense of humor about both. She clearly doesn't take herself too seriously, and that kind of self-awareness is a big part of what makes her one of the more relatable personalities in sports television. She comes across as someone you could easily share a beer with after the game.

Thompson's First Marriage

The 44-year-old broadcaster has been married twice. Her first marriage came when she was 25, and she has kept most of the details about it private over the years.

Still, she hasn't always spoken harshly about that relationship. In a 2016 Facebook post, Thompson gave her first ex-husband credit for lifting her spirits during a difficult stretch.

"When your ex-husband helps you through sadness and makes you smile. He's a hot mess and I appreciate him so much. Ladies, by the way he's single! I'll hook you up."

At first glance, the post seems to contradict her claim that all of her exes are bad. Then comes the "hot mess" line and the playful offer to set him up, which fits right in with the humor she brought to the Prime Video desk.

A Short Second Marriage

Thompson tied the knot again in December 2020, marrying sports agent and former college baseball player Kyle Thousand. That marriage didn't last long. In April 2022, Thompson filed for divorce, citing irreconcilable differences.

Since then, she has been clear that she is done with marriage in the legal sense. Responding to a fan during an Instagram Q&A, she wrote:

"No, I will never legally get married again. I won't sign any paperwork. But happy to have a party and celebrate how much I love Steve with friends and family."

Finding Happiness on Her Own Terms

The "Steve" in that post is Steve Cundari, Thompson's current boyfriend. She has spoken openly about how her outlook on relationships has changed, including during an appearance on Kylie Kelce's "Not Gonna Lie" podcast.

"I married the wrong people, plural. Just being with a man who is kind and doesn't take from me is commitment enough for me."

It is a refreshingly honest perspective, and it puts her Thursday night joke in context. Thompson isn't bitter about her past. She has simply made peace with it, and she is comfortable enough to laugh about it in front of a national audience.

The Bottom Line

The Bears earned a big win on Thursday, but Thompson earned some fans of her own. Her offhand remark about her ex-husbands was unexpected, unfiltered and genuinely funny—the kind of moment that makes a broadcast memorable long after the final score fades.

Based on everything she has shared, Thompson is happy where she is, with Cundari by her side and no marriage license in sight. And if that means more honest, unscripted moments on Prime Video's postgame show, viewers certainly won't be complaining.
excerpt: Amazon Prime Video host Charissa Thompson stole the Thursday Night Football postgame show with an unscripted quip about her ex-husbands, offering a rare unfiltered moment that resonated far beyond the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots.
